h: Stone dodos, a racehorse and a temple to the winds
p: The gardens owe much of their character to Edith, Lady Londonderry, who created them in the 1920s. She had a playful streak, and nowhere shows it better than the Dodo Terrace, where stone creatures, including dodos, monkeys and other animals, represent members of her social circle, a group she called the Ark Club. Spotting them all is great fun for kids and grown-ups alike.
Look out for the Shamrock Garden, with its Irish harp-shaped topiary, and the Italian and Spanish gardens near the house. The lake walk is a peaceful loop that shows off the wider estate.

Inside the house, one of the highlights is Hambletonian, Rubbing Down, a famous painting of a racehorse by George Stubbs. Even if you are not into art, it is a striking piece, and it gives you an insight into the family's love of horses.
On a hill overlooking the lough stands the Temple of the Winds, an 18th-century banqueting house with gorgeous views across the water.

Allow at least half a day. Strangford Lough is a wildlife hotspot, especially in winter, when huge numbers of brent geese arrive. Nearby, the ruins of Grey Abbey are worth a look, while Scrabo Tower stands on a hill above Newtownards with views across the lough. At the southern tip of the Ards Peninsula, Exploris aquarium at Portaferry is a good family add-on.
